questions.stem_text:
Explain how an estimate of the age of a rock is made on the basisof the radioactive
elements present.

options.A: By assessing the fossil content found within the rock layers
options.B: By comparing the density of the rock to a known age database
options.C: By examining the color and texture of the rock
options.D: By counting the layers of the rock
options.E: By measuring the amount of carbon-14 remaining in the rock

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - By assessing the fossil content found within the rock layers

questions.stem_text: What are some of the cues used by animal in migrating?

options.A: Animals use the sound of the ocean waves for directional cues in migration.
options.B: Animals rely solely on memory from previous migrations.
options.C: Animals migrate based on the patterns of the stars alone.
options.D: Animals follow changes in air pressure for migration.
options.E: Animals use temperature changes for migration.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Animals use the sound of the ocean waves for directional cues in migration.

questions.stem_text: How do bacteria develop drug resistance?

options.A: Antibiotic resistance arises from bacteria absorbing nutrients that counteract the drug
options.B: Resistance develops due to prolonged exposure to antibiotics
options.C: Bacteria develop a natural immunity to drugs over time
options.D: Bacteria develop resistance through spontaneous generation without exposure to antibiotics
options.E: Drug resistance is caused solely by the use of antibacterial hand sanitizers

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Antibiotic resistance arises from bacteria absorbing nutrients that counteract the drug

questions.stem_text: Are hepatitis G virus and TT virus involved in cryptogenic chronic liver disease?
questions.answer_explanation: In Southern Italy, hepatitis G virus infection is widespread among patients with chronic hepatitis, independently of parenteral risk factors. Its frequency in subjects with cryptogenic liver disease parallels that observed in hepatitis C virus chronic liver disease, thus ruling out an aetiologic role of hepatitis G virus. TT virus infection is uncommon in patients with cryptogenic or hepatitis C virus-related liver disease who do not have a history of parenteral exposure.

questions.stem_text: Is there any relationship between streptococcal infection and multiple sclerosis?
questions.answer_explanation: These findings indicate that a relationship between multiple sclerosis and streptococcal infections may exist, but to acquire a better understanding of the role of group A streptococci in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis, more studies with animal models are necessary.

questions.stem_text: Can medical students contribute to quality assurance programmes in day surgery?
questions.answer_explanation: Our study confirms that students are able to identify QA issues and propose solutions. We recommend that students have a formally recognized place in day surgery QA programmes, to close the QA loop and to adequately prepare them for medical practice in the 21 st century.

questions.stem_text: Does pain intensity predict a poor opioid response in cancer patients?
questions.answer_explanation: Baseline pain intensity does not predict the outcome after an appropriate opioid titration. It is likely that non-homogeneous pain treatment would have biased the outcome of a previous work.

questions.stem_text: Eyelid-parotid metastasis: do we screen for coexisting masses?
questions.answer_explanation: These cases illustrate that tumours involving eyelids and parotid glands can present simultaneously or sequentially, and either of these structures could be the focus of primary or metastatic tumour. The important message for oculoplastic and parotid surgeons is to routinely assess both the periocular and parotid area when patients present with a mass in either structure.
